idiom_name: opaque type + one create function per creation path (order_open / order_rehydrate) with a status enum
implementation_notes: C has no constructors, no access control and no exception type, so the DDD factory is hand-written: declare an incomplete struct in the header, define it in the .c file, and expose one create function per creation path that validates every input before calloc() and reports failure through a status enum or an out-parameter. What replaces the classic factory class is that create function plus the opaque boundary - clients can hold only order_t * and speak the header's API; the full multi-product factory (function-pointer tables choosing an implementation) is reserved for cases where the product type itself must vary at run time.
pitfalls: The opaque boundary is the whole enforcement: exposing the struct definition (or a private header) lets callers allocate and fill an order themselves, bypassing validation.
A create function that fails after partial allocation must free everything it already built; validate all inputs first and allocate second so there is nothing to unwind.
Document single ownership and take order_t ** in destroy so the caller's pointer is nulled, making use-after-free visible instead of silent.
